text: さる程に、兵衞佐は足柄の山を打越えて、駿河國黄瀬川にこそ著給へ。甲斐信濃の源氏ども馳來て一つになる。浮島が原にて、勢汰あり。廿萬騎とぞ記いたる。常陸源氏佐竹太郎が雜色、主の使に文持て京へ上るを、平家の先陣上總守忠清是を留て、持たる文を奪取り明て見れば、女房の許への文也。苦かるまじとて取せてけり。「抑兵衞佐殿の勢、いか程有ぞ。」と問へば、「凡そ八日九日の道に、はたとつゞいて、野も山も海も河も武者で候。下臈は四五百千迄こそ、物の數をば知て候へ共其より上は知らぬ候。多いやらう少いやらうをば知候はず。昨日黄瀬川にて、人の申つるは、源氏の御勢二十萬騎とこそ申候つれ。」上總守是を聞いて、「あはれ大將軍の御心の延させ給たる程、口惜い事候はず。今一日も先に討手を下させ給ひたらば、足柄の山越えて、八箇國へ御出候はゞ、畠山が一族、大庭兄弟、などか參らで候べき。是等だにも參りなば、坂東には靡かぬ草木も候まじ。」と、後悔すれども甲斐ぞなき。

annotation.translation: In this manner, the Hyoe-no-suke crossed the Hakone Mountains and arrived at the Kise River in Suruga Province. The Genji of Kai and Shinano galloped forth and united. At Ukishima Field, there was a great battle. It is recorded that there were two hundred thousand horsemen. The mixed troops of Hitachi Genji, Satake Taro, bearing a letter as a messenger for their lord, went up to the capital; the Heike's vanguard, Kozuke-no-mori Tadakiyo, stopped them, snatched the letter, and opened it to read. It was a letter addressed to the women's quarters. Thinking it should not be taken, they seized it. "By the way, how great is Lord Hyoe-no-suke's force?" he asked. "Roughly, on the road of eight or nine days, they follow one after another; the fields, mountains, seas, and rivers are filled with warriors. The common soldiers number perhaps four to five hundred thousand, but we do not know those above that. We do not know whether they are many or few. Yesterday at Kise River, someone reported that the Genji's force is two hundred thousand horsemen." Hearing this, Kozuke-no-mori said, "Alas, how grievous that the Great General's heart has been delayed so long! If only he would dispatch the vanguard one day sooner, and cross the Hakone Mountains and enter the eight provinces, would not the Hatakeyama clan and the Otomo brothers come? Even if they came, there would be no grass or trees in Bandō that would not bow before them." Yet, even as he regretted it, there was no hope in Kai.

text: 又大將軍權亮少將維盛、東國の案内者とて、長井齋藤別當實盛を召て、「やや實盛、汝程の強弓精兵、八箇國に如何程有ぞ。」と問ひ給へば、齋藤別當あざ笑て申けるは、「左候へば、君は實盛を大矢と思召し候か。僅に十三束こそ仕り候へ。實盛程射候者は八箇國に幾らも候。大矢と申す定の者の、十五束に劣て引は候はず、弓の強さも、したゝかなる者五六人して張り候。かゝる精兵共が射候へば、鎧の二三兩をも重ねて、容易う射て徹し候也。大名一人と申は勢の少い定、五百騎に劣るは候はず。馬に乘つれば落る道を知らず。惡所を馳れども、馬を倒さず。軍は又親も討れよ、子も討れよ、死ぬれば乘越々々戰ふ候。西國の軍と申は親討れぬれば孝養し、忌明て寄せ、子討れぬれば、其思ひ歎きに、寄候はず。兵粮米盡ぬれば春は田作り、秋は刈収て寄せ、夏は熱しと云ひ、冬は寒しと嫌ひ候。東國には、惣て其儀候はず。甲斐信濃の源氏共、案内は知て候。富士のすそより搦手にやまはり候らん。かう申せば、君を憶せさせ參せんとて申とや思召し候らん。其儀には候はず。軍は勢には依らず、策に依るとこそ申傳て候へ。實盛今度の軍に命生て再都へ參るべしとも覺候はず。」と申ければ、平家の兵共是を聞て、皆震ひわなゝきあへり。

annotation.translation: Again, when the Great General, the Right Assistant, and the Junior General, Tomomori, summoned Saigō Saitō Betto Mochimori as a guide from the Eastern Provinces and asked, 'Mochimori, how many such strong bows and elite soldiers are there throughout the eight provinces?' the Saitō Betto laughed and replied, 'If that is what you think, do you consider Mochimori a great bow? He can only draw thirteen bundles. There are many in the eight provinces who draw like Mochimori. The great bow, the standard of a certain type, cannot be drawn if it is inferior to fifteen bundles; even the strength of the bow, there are only five or six such powerful individuals who can draw it. When such elite soldiers shoot, they can pierce through two or three layers of armor with ease. A great lord, the standard of having a small force, cannot be inferior to five hundred cavalry. When mounted on a horse, they do not know the way to fall. Even if they gallop through dangerous places, they do not let their horses fall. The Eastern army, furthermore, whether their parents are killed or their children are killed, when they die, they fight by trampling over them. The Western army, however, if their parents are killed, they practice filial piety; they gather only after the mourning period is over. If their children are killed, they do not gather, overcome by their sorrow and grief. If their provisions and rice are exhausted, in spring they till the fields, in autumn they harvest and gather, in summer they complain of the heat, and in winter they complain of the cold. This is not the case in the Eastern Provinces. The Genji of Kai and Shinano know the way of guidance. They will surely circle around from the base of Mount Fuji to the rear. If I say this, do you think I am saying it to make you remember me? It is not so. The army does not rely on numbers but on strategy, as is handed down. Mochimori does not even think of offering his life in this campaign to return to the capital.' Upon hearing this, the Heike soldiers all trembled and wept.
annotation.summary: Again, when the Great General, the Right Assistant, and the Junior General, Tomomori, summoned Saigō Saitō Betto Mochimori as a guide from the Eastern Provinces and asked, 'Mochimori, how many such strong bows and elite soldiers are there throughout the eight provinces?' the Saitō Betto laughed and replied, 'If that is what you think, do you consider Mochimori a great bow? He can only draw thirteen bundles. There are many in the eight provinces who draw like Mochimori. The great bow, the standard of a certain type, cannot be drawn if it is inferior to fifteen bundles; even the strength of the bow, there are only five or six such powerful individuals who can draw it. When such elite soldiers shoot, they can pierce through two or three layers of armor with ease. A great lord, the standard of having a small force, cannot be inferior to five hundred cavalry. When mounted on a horse, they do not know the way to fall. Even if they gallop through dangerous places, they do not let their horses fall. The Eastern army, furthermore, whether their parents are killed or their children are killed, when they die, they fight by trampling over them. The Western army, however, if their parents are killed, they practice filial piety; they gather only after the mourning period is over. If their children are killed, they do not gather, overcome by their sorrow and grief. If their provisions and rice are exhausted, in spring they till the fields, in autumn they harvest and gather, in summer they complain of the heat, and in winter they complain of the cold. This is not the case in the Eastern Provinces. The Genji of Kai and Shinano know the way of guidance. They will surely circle around from the base of Mount Fuji to the rear. If I say this, do you think I am saying it to make you remember me? It is not so. The army does not rely on numbers but on strategy, as is handed down. Mochimori does not even think of offering his life in this campaign to return to the capital.' Upon hearing this, the Heike soldiers all trembled and wept.

text: さる程に、十月二十三日にもなりぬ。明日は源平富士川にて、矢合と定めたりけるに、夜に入て、平家の方より源氏の陣を見渡せば、伊豆駿河の人民百姓等が、軍に怖て、或は野に入り山に隱れ、或は舟に取乘て、海河に浮び、營の火見えけるを、平家の兵共「あなおびただしの源氏の陣の遠火の多さよ。げにも誠に野も山も海も河も、皆敵で有けり。如何せん。」とぞあわてける。其夜の夜半ばかり、富士の沼に幾らもむれ居たりける水鳥共が、何にか驚きたりけん、只一度にはと立ける羽音の、大風雷などの樣に聞えければ、平家の兵共、「すはやげんじの大勢の寄するは。齋藤別當が申つる樣に、定めて搦手もまはるらん。取籠められては叶ふまじ。爰をば引いて、尾張河、州俣を防げや。」とて、取る物も取敢ず、我先にとぞ落行ける。餘に遽て噪いで弓取る者は矢を知らず、矢取る者は弓を知らず、人の馬には我乘り、わが馬をば人に乘らる。或は繋いだる馬に騎て株を繞る事限なし。近き宿々より迎へ取て遊びける遊君遊女共、或は頭蹴破れ、腰蹈折れて、喚叫ぶ者多かりけり。

annotation.translation: So it came to pass that the twenty-third day of the tenth month arrived. It had been decided that the next day the Genji and Heike would engage in battle with arrows at Fujikawa. As night fell, the Heike, gazing across at the Genji camp, saw that the common people of Izu and Suruga, terrified by the army, were either entering the fields and hiding in the mountains, or boarding boats and floating upon the seas and rivers. Seeing the fires of the camp, the Heike soldiers exclaimed, "How incredibly numerous are the distant fires of the Genji camp! Truly, both the fields and the mountains, the seas and the rivers, are all filled with enemies. What shall we do?" They were in a panic. Around the middle of that night, the waterfowl that had gathered in great numbers in the marshes of Mount Fuji were startled by some cause; their wings beating in a single instant were heard like a great wind and thunder. The Heike soldiers said, "Hastily, the great force of the Genji is approaching. As Saitei no Betto predicted, surely they are turning to attack our rear. If we are surrounded, there is no hope. Let us withdraw and defend Owarikawa and Shumata." Without even taking their belongings, each striving to be first, they fled in disorder. In their great haste, those who grasped bows did not know how to use arrows, and those who grasped arrows did not know how to use bows; they mounted other people's horses, and other people mounted their horses. Some rode their tethered horses in circles around the posts without limit. The young men and courtesans who came from nearby inns to welcome and entertain them were many who had their heads kicked in, their waists trodden upon, and who cried out in terror.

annotation.translation: On the following 24th day, in the hour of the Rabbit, a great army of 200,000 horsemen of the Minamoto advanced upon the Fuji River; so loud was their war cry that it echoed in the sky and shook the earth, and they raised the shout three times.

text: 平家の方には、音もせず。人を遣はして見せければ、「皆落て候。」と申す。或は敵の忘たる鎧取て參りたる者も有り。或は敵の捨たる大幕取て參りたる者も有り。「敵の陣には蠅だにも翔り候はず。」と申す。兵衞佐、馬より降り、甲を脱ぎ、手水鵜飼をして、王城の方を伏拜み、「是は全く頼朝が私の高名にあらず、八幡第菩薩の御計也。」とぞ宣ひける。やがて打取る所なればとて、駿河國をば一條次郎忠頼、遠江をば安田三郎義定に預けらる。平家續いても攻べけれども後もさすが覺束なしとて浮島原より引退き、相摸國へぞ歸られける。海道宿々の遊君遊女ども、「あな忌々し。射手の大將軍の矢一つだに射ずして、逃上り給ふうたてさよ。軍には見逃と云事をだに心憂き事にこそするに、是は聞にげし給ひたり。」と笑ひあへり。落書共多かりけり。都の大將軍をば宗盛と云ひ、討手の大將をば權亮と云ふ間、平家をひら屋によみなして、

annotation.translation: To the Heike side, there was not even a sound. When people were sent to look, they said, "They have all fallen." There were also those who had brought back enemy armor they had forgotten, and there were those who had brought back enemy large curtains they had discarded. "Even a single fly does not fly into the enemy camp," they said. Eimon-no-sa descended from his horse, removed his armor, performed the hand-washing ritual, bowed his head toward the Imperial Capital, and declared, "This is entirely not due to Yoritomo's reputation, but to the Hachiman Daibosatsu's plan." Since it was a place where one should soon be struck, Suruga Province was entrusted to Ichijo-no-jiro Tadayori, and Totomi Province to Yasuda-no-sabro Yoshisada. Although the Heike continued to fight, they could not hold their ground, and so they withdrew from Ukishima-hara and returned to Sagami Province. The wandering youths and courtesans at the inns along the coastal road laughed, saying, "Oh, how detestable! The great general of the archers did not even shoot a single arrow, yet he was allowed to flee in triumph! In an army, it is said that one should not let the enemy escape, yet this is a matter that has indeed been heard of." There were many such graffiti. They called the great general of the capital Munemori, and the great general of the attacking force Gonryo, and they read the Heike as "Hira-ya."

text:
同十一月八日、大將軍權亮少將維盛、福原の新都へ上りつく。入道相國大に怒て、
「大將軍權亮少將維盛をば鬼界が島へ流すべし、侍大將上總守忠清をば死罪に行へ。」
とぞ宣ひける。同九日平家の侍共、老少參會して、「忠清が死罪の事、いかゞ有ら
ん。」と評定す。中に主馬判官盛國進出でて申けるは、「忠清は昔より不覺人とは承
り及ばず、あれが十八歳と覺え候、鳥羽殿の寶藏に五畿内の惡黨二人、迯籠て候しを、
寄て搦めうと申す者候はざりしに、此忠清白晝に唯一人築地を越え、はね入て、一人
をば討取り、一人をば生捕て、後代に名を揚たりし者にて候。今度の不覺は、徒事と
も覺え候はず。是に附ても、能々兵亂の御愼候べし。」とぞ申ける。

annotation.translation: On the eighth day of that same November, the Great General, the Right Minister, the Junior Minister Tomomori, arrived at the new capital of Fukuhara. The Cloistered Retired Emperor and Great Minister was angry and declared, 'The Great General, the Right Minister, the Junior Minister Tomomori should be exiled to the island of Kikai; the Senior General, the Governor of Kazusa, Tadanori, should be sentenced to death.' This was proclaimed. On the ninth day of that same month, the warriors of the Taira clan, young and old, gathered to deliberate: 'What shall be done regarding Tadanori's death sentence?' Among them, the Main Horse Keeper, the Judge Mochikuni, stepped forward and said, 'It is not my understanding that Tadanori has ever been an unconscious man; he appears to be eighteen years of age. Two evil bandits from the Five Provinces had taken refuge in the treasury of the Imperial Palace of Toba, and I was told that they had not yet been caught. Yet, this Tadanori, in broad daylight, crossed the fortress wall alone, leaped in, killed one of them, and captured the other alive, thereby gaining a reputation for posterity. It does not seem that his lapse in this instance was merely a matter of negligence. Therefore, let us also be extremely careful in matters of military disorder.' This was said.

Though he was heard to be the Great General of the Attackers, no one had yet emerged to lead. "What reward is this?" the people whispered among themselves.

text: 昔將門追討の爲に、平將軍貞盛、田原藤太秀里、うけ給て坂東へ發向したりしかども、將門容易う亡難かりしかば、重て討手を下すべしと、公卿僉議あて、宇治民部卿忠文、清原重藤、軍監と云ふ官を給て下られけり。駿河國清見關に宿したりける夜、彼重藤、漫々たる海上を遠見して、「漁舟火影寒うして浪を燒き、驛路鈴聲夜山をすぐ」と云ふ唐歌を高らかに口ずさみ給へば、忠文優に覺えて、感涙をぞ流されける。さる程に將門をば、貞盛秀里が終に討取てけり。其頭を持せて上る程に、清見關にて行逢うたり。其より先後の大將軍打連て上洛す。貞盛秀里に勸賞行はれける時、忠文重藤にも勸賞有べきかと、公卿僉議有り。九條右丞相師輔公の申させ給ひけるは、「坂東へ討手は向うたりと云へども、將門容易う亡ひ難き處に、此人共仰を蒙て、關の東へ赴く時、朝敵既に亡びたり。さればなどか勸賞無るべき。」と申させ給へども、其時の執柄小野宮殿、「『疑しきをば成す事なかれ』と禮記の文に候へば。」とて、遂になさせ給はず。忠文是を口惜事にして、「小野宮殿の御末をば、奴に見なさん。九條殿の御末には、何の世迄も守護神と成ん。」と誓ひつゝ、干死にこそし給ひけれ。されば九條殿の御末は、目出たう榮させ給へども、小野宮殿の御末には、然るべき人も坐さず、今は絶果給ひけるにこそ。

annotation.translation: In ancient times, for the purpose of subduing Shōmon, General Taira no Sadamori, Taira no Hidehira of Tawara, and others were summoned and sent to the Kantō region, yet because Shōmon was difficult to kill, it was decided by a joint deliberation of the court nobles that more troops should be dispatched, and Minabe no Ason Tadahito and Kiyohara no Shigefuji were appointed as military inspectors. One night while they were staying at the Kiyomi Pass in Suruga Province, Shigefuji, gazing out over the vast sea, loudly hummed a Chinese poem: 'The fishing boats' lanterns burn coldly, lighting the waves; the bell of the postal road cuts through the night mountains.' Tadahito, having keenly remembered it, was moved to tears. Thus, Shōmon was finally slain by Sadamori and Hidehira. When they carried his head and ascended, they encountered each other at the Kiyomi Pass. From that time onward, successive great generals marched to the capital. When commendations were to be bestowed upon Sadamori and Hidehira, the court nobles deliberated whether commendations should also be given to Tadahito and Shigefuji. The Right Minister of the Left, the Duke of Kujō, Motosuke, declared, 'Although troops were sent to the Kantō region, by the time these men arrived in the Eastern Provinces, the enemy of the court had already been destroyed; therefore, how could commendations be lacking?' Yet, the powerful regent of the time, the Duke of Ononomiya, stated, 'The Analects of Rites say, "When there is doubt, do not proceed."' Consequently, he was not allowed to bestow them. Tadahito regarded this as a grievance, vowing, 'May the descendants of the Duke of Ononomiya become slaves, but may the descendants of the Duke of Kujō be guardians for all generations.' And so he died in despair. Therefore, although the descendants of the Duke of Kujō have prospered, no worthy person has sat in the line of the Duke of Ononomiya, and now their line has come to an end.

text: さる程に入道相國の四男、頭中將重衡、左近衞中將に成給ふ。同十一月十三日福原には、内裏造出して、主上御遷幸有り。大嘗會あるべかりしかども、大嘗會は十月の末、東河に御幸して、御禊有り。大内の北の野に齋場所を作て、神服神具を調ふ。大極殿の前、龍尾道の壇下に、迴立殿を建て、御湯をめす。同壇の竝に、大嘗宮を作て、神膳を備ふ。宸宴有り。御遊有り。大極殿にて大禮有り。清暑堂にて御神樂有り。豊樂院にて宴會あり。然を此福原の新都には、大極殿も無ければ、大禮行ふべき處もなし。清暑堂無れば、御神樂奏すべき樣もなし。豊樂院も無れば、宴會も行はれず。今年は唯新嘗會五節許有るべきよし、公卿僉議有て、猶新嘗の祭をば、舊都の神祇官にして遂られけり。

annotation.translation: Accordingly, the fourth son of the retired Emperor Daijo, Head Captain Shigehira, was appointed Left Inner Guard Captain. On the thirteenth day of the same month, the Imperial Palace was constructed in Fuhara, and His Majesty proceeded to reside there. Although the Great Harvest Festival ought to have been held, the Great Harvest Festival had taken place at the end of October, when His Majesty visited Higashigawa and underwent purification. A ritual precinct was established in the northern fields of the Imperial Palace, where the sacred garments and utensils were prepared. Before the Great Hall of State, on the terrace below the Dragon Tail Road, a Hall of Return was built, and a sacred bath was prepared. Adjacent to this terrace, the Great Harvest Palace was constructed, and the sacred meal was readied. An imperial banquet was held. A royal excursion took place. A great ceremony was held in the Great Hall of State. A sacred music performance was held in the Clear Summer Hall. A feast was held at Toyoraku-in. However, in this new capital of Fuhara, there was no Great Hall of State, nor any place where a great ceremony could be conducted. Without the Clear Summer Hall, there was no arrangement for performing sacred music. Without Toyoraku-in, the feast could not be held either. This year, it was agreed upon by all the court nobles that only the New Harvest Festival would be held for about five days, and consequently, the New Harvest festival was concluded at the Shrine Bureau in the old capital.

text: 五節は、淨見原の當時、吉野宮にして、月白く風烈しかりし夜、御心を澄しつゝ琴を彈給しに、神女あま下り、五度袖を飜す。是ぞ五節の始なる。

annotation.translation: The Five Movements occurred at the time of Jōken-Gen in the Yoshino Palace, on a night when the moon was bright and the wind was fierce. With his mind clear, he played the koto; then a divine maiden descended from heaven, and she turned her sleeves five times. This is the beginning of the Five Movements.

text: 今度の都遷をば、君も臣も御歎有り。山奈良を始て、諸寺諸社に至る迄、然べからざる由一同に訴申間、さしも横紙を破るゝ太政入道も、さらば都還有るべしとて京中ひしめきあへり。

annotation.translation: As for this upcoming relocation of the capital, both you and the ministers are greatly distressed. Since the plea was made collectively by all, from Mount Kamo and Mount Nara all the way to every temple and shrine, that such a thing should not be done, even the powerful Daijō-daijin, who usually breaks through any obstruction, declared that the capital must be restored, and thus the people of Kyoto thronged together.

text: 同十二月二日、俄に都還有けり。新都は北は山にそひて高く、南は海近くして下れり。波の音常は喧く、鹽風烈しき所也。されば新院いつとなく、御惱のみしげかりければ、急ぎ福原を出させ給ふ。攝政殿を始奉て、太政大臣以下の公卿殿上人我も／＼と供奉せらる。入道相國を始として平家一門の公卿殿上人我先にとぞ上られける。誰か心憂かりつる新都に、片時も殘るべき。去る六月より屋ども壞よせ、資材雜具運び下し、形の如く取立たりつるに、又物狂はしう、都還有ければ、何の沙汰にも及ばず、打捨々々上られけり。各すみかも無くして、八幡、賀茂、嵯峨、太秦、西山、東山の片邊について、御堂のくわい廊、社の拜殿などに、立宿てぞ然るべき人々もましましける。

annotation.translation: In the twelfth month of that year, they suddenly departed for the capital. The new capital was high on the north side, leaning against the mountains, and low on the south side, near the sea. The sound of the waves was always loud, and the salty wind was sharp; such was the place. Therefore, as the Emperor's sorrow grew ever more intense, without delay he commanded the departure from Fuhara. The Regent's residence was the first to be prepared, and the Dajō-daijin and other court nobles and high priests followed one after another. Beginning with the Retired Emperor, the Taira clan's nobles and high priests competed to be the first to ascend. Who could remain in the new capital even for a moment, so full of sorrow? Since last June, the houses had been dismantled, materials and miscellaneous goods had been carried down, and everything had been arranged as if it were a formal undertaking, yet it was again a mad rush, for they suddenly departed for the capital. Nothing could be properly arranged; everything was simply abandoned, and they departed. With no shelter left anywhere, even those who should have been there were forced to take up lodging in the verandas of temples, the prayer halls of shrines, and other places at the outskirts of Hachiman, Kamo, Saga, Uda, the Western Hills, and the Eastern Hills.

text: 今度の都遷の本意を如何にと云ふに、舊都は南都北嶺近くして、聊の事にも春日の神木、日吉の神輿など言て亂りがはし。福原は山隔たり江重て、程もさすが遠ければ、左樣の事たやすからじとて、入道相國の計ひ出されたりけるとかや。

annotation.translation: As for the true purpose of this relocation of the capital, one might say: 'The old capital is close to the Southern Capital and the Northern Ridge, and minor incidents can easily lead to disturbances such as those involving the sacred tree of Kasuga or the portable shrines of Hie; since Fukuhara is separated by mountains and blocked by rivers, and is certainly far away, such things would not occur so easily; thus, this plan was devised by the Retired Emperor and the State Minister, as it is said.'

text: 同十二月二十三日、近江源氏の背きしを攻んとて、大將軍には左兵衞督知盛、薩摩守忠度、都合其勢二萬餘騎で、近江國へ發向して、山本、柏木、錦古里など云ふ溢れ源氏共一々に皆攻落し、やがて美濃尾張へ越え給ふ。

annotation.translation: On the 23rd day of the twelfth month of the same year, to attack the treacherous Minamoto of Ōmi, the Grand General, Sakanoe-no-Tsuwamono no Tachibana no Moritsune, along with Satsuma-no-Kami Tadanori, with a total force of over twenty thousand cavalry, advanced toward Ōmi Province and utterly defeated the overflowing Minamoto, including Yamamoto, Kashiwagi, and Kinokuri, and then crossed over to Mino and Owari.

text: 都には又高倉宮園城寺へ入御の時、南都の大衆同心して、剩へ御迎に參る候、是以て朝敵なり。されば南都をも三井寺をも攻らるべしといふ程こそ在けれ、奈良の大衆おびただしく蜂起す。攝政殿より「存の旨あらば、幾度も奏聞にこそ及ばめ。」と仰下されけれ共一切用たてまつらず。有官の別當忠成を御使に下されたりければ、「しや乘物より取て引落せ、髻切れ。」と騒動する間、忠成色を失て迯上る。次に右衞門佐親雅を下さる。是をも「髻切れ。」と大衆ひしめきければ、取る物も取敢ず、逃上る。其時は勸學院の雜色二人が、髻切れけり。

annotation.translation: Furthermore, at the time the Emperor entered the Enryaku-ji Temple in the capital, the multitude of the Southern Capital joined together to meet the Imperial procession in excess; therefore, they are considered enemies of the court. Consequently, there was a time when it was said that both the Southern Capital and Miidera Temple should be attacked, and the multitude of Nara rose up in great numbers. The Regent's Palace issued the command: "If you wish to proceed, you may present your report repeatedly." Yet, no heed was given to this. When a high-ranking official, Betto Tadanari, was sent as an envoy, the multitude clamored, "Take him down from his palanquin and cut off his topknot!" In the midst of this commotion, Tadanari lost his composure and fled. Next, Uemon-no-suke Chikamasa was sent. The multitude again crowded about him, shouting, "Cut off his topknot!" Unable to grasp even a single item to defend himself, he fled. At that time, two low-ranking monks of the Ken'ōin Temple were the ones who had their topknots cut off.

text: 又南都には大なる毬杖の玉作て、是は平相國の頭と名附て、「打て、踏め。」などぞ申ける。「詞の漏し易は殃を招く媒也。詞の愼まざるは、破れを取る道也。」と云へり。此入道相國と申は、かけまくも忝く當今の外祖にて坐ます。其をか樣に申ける南都の大衆、凡は天魔の所爲とぞ見えたりける。

annotation.translation: Furthermore, in the Southern Capital, there was a great ball made of jade, which was named the 'Head of the Lord of the State of Hira.' They would say, 'Strike it, tread upon it.' But it was said, 'A word carelessly let slip invites calamity; a word not spoken with caution is the path to ruin.' This monk, referred to as the Lord of the State, was none other than the current Emperor's maternal grandfather, who sat upon the throne. The multitude of the Southern Capital, hearing such things, concluded that it was all the work of the Heavenly Demon.

text:
入道相國か樣の事共傳聞給ひて、爭か好しと思はるべき。且々南都の狼藉を靜めんとて、備中國の住人瀬尾太郎兼康、大和國の檢非所に補せらる。兼康五百餘騎で南都へ發向す。「相構て、衆徒は狼藉を致すとも、汝等は致すべからず。物具なせそ。弓箭な帶しそ。」とて向はれたりけるに、大衆かゝる内議をば知らず、兼康が餘勢六十餘人搦取て、一々に皆頸を斬て、猿澤の池の端にぞ懸竝べたる。入道相國大に怒て、
「さらば南都を攻よや。」とて、大將軍には頭中將重衡、副將軍には中宮亮通盛、都
合其勢四萬餘騎で南都へ發向す。大衆老少嫌はず七千餘人甲の緒をしめ、奈良坂、般
若寺、二箇所の路を掘切て、堀ほり垣楯かき、逆茂木引て待かけたり。平家は四萬餘
騎を二手に分て、奈良坂、般若寺、二箇所の城郭に押寄て、鬨をどとつくる。大衆は
皆歩立打物なり。官軍は馬にてかけまはしかけまはし、あそここゝに追懸／＼指つめ
引つめ散々に射ければ、防ぐ所の大衆數を盡いて討れにけり。卯刻に矢合して一日戰
ひ暮す。夜に入て、奈良坂、般若寺、二箇所の城郭共に破れぬ。落行く衆徒の中に、
坂四郎永覺と云ふ惡僧あり。打物持ても弓箭を取ても力の強さも七大寺十五大寺に勝
たり。萌黄威の腹巻の上に、黒絲威の鎧を重てぞ著たりける。帽子甲に五枚甲の緒を
しめて、左右の手には茅の葉の樣に反たる白柄の大長刀、黒漆の大太刀持つまゝに、
同宿十餘人前後にたて、てがいの門より打て出でたり。是ぞ暫支たる。多くの官兵、馬の足薙れて討れにけり。されども官軍は大勢にて、入替入替攻ければ、永覺が前後左右に防ぐ所の同宿皆討れぬ。永覺只獨猛けれども、後あらはになりければ、南を指いて落ぞ行く。

annotation.translation: The Ingress Daisan, the Great Minister, heard various matters and thought, 'How good it would be to quell the depredations in the Southern Capital.' Thus, Seo Taro Kaneyasu, a resident of Bizen Province, was appointed to the position of Inspector in Yamato Province. Kaneyasu, leading over five hundred cavalry, set out for the Southern Capital. He said, 'Even if the monks commit depredations, you must not do so. Do not prepare weapons. Do not carry bows and arrows.' As they were advancing on this pretext, the common people, unaware of such internal deliberations, were attacked by Kaneyasu's remaining forces of over sixty men, who cut off the necks of each one individually and hung them in a row at the edge of Sarusawa Pond. The Ingress Daisan became greatly enraged and said, 'Then let us attack the Southern Capital.' He appointed the Grand General, Head of the Middle Command, Tadanori, and the Vice-General, the Middle Palace's Magistrate, Tsunemori. Together with a force of over forty thousand cavalry, they set out for the Southern Capital. The common people, young and old alike, over seven thousand in number, tightened their armor laces, dug trenches at two locations, Nara-zaka and Hannya-ji, built walls and ramparts, and set up inverted palisades to await them. The Taira divided their forty thousand cavalry into two groups and advanced upon the two fortifications at Nara-zaka and Hannya-ji, raising a great battle cry. The common people were all foot soldiers armed with polearms. The imperial forces rode around, charging here and there, shooting arrows with such intensity that they pierced and scattered the defenders, killing all who tried to hold the line. At dawn, the archery duel began, and the battle continued until dusk. By nightfall, the fortifications at both Nara-zaka and Hannya-ji remained unbroken. Among the retreating monks was an evil monk named Sakano-shiro Eikaku. Whether wielding a polearm or a bow and arrow, his strength surpassed that of the monks of the Seven Great Temples and the Fifteen Great Temples. He wore a black silk armor over a yellow-green lacquered cuirass. He had fastened the laces of a five-plate helmet to his cap and, in both hands, held long white-handled swords resembling bamboo leaves, along with a large black-lacquered sword, while standing with over ten fellow monks from the same lodging. They burst forth from the main gate. This briefly held them back. Many imperial soldiers were trampled by horses and slain. Nevertheless, the imperial forces, being numerous, attacked repeatedly, and all of Eikaku's companions who defended him from all sides were killed. Though Eikaku fought alone with great ferocity, his position became untenable, and he turned south to retreat.

text: 夜軍に成て、暗は暗し、大將軍頭中將重衡、般若寺の門の前に打立て、「火を出せ。」と宣ふ程こそ在けれ。平家の勢の中に播磨國の住人福井庄の下司、次郎太夫友方と云ふ者、楯を破り續松にして、在家に火をぞ懸けたりける。十二月二十八日の夜なりければ、風は烈しゝ、火本は一つなりけれども、吹迷ふ風に、多くの伽藍に吹かけたり。恥をも思ひ、名をも惜む程の者は、奈良坂にて討死し、般若寺にて討れにけり。行歩に叶へる者は、吉野十津川の方へ落ゆく。歩も得ぬ老僧や、尋常なる修學者、兒ども、女童部は、大佛殿、山階寺の内へ我先にとぞ迯行ける。大佛殿の二階の上には、千餘人昇り上り、敵の續くを上せじと階をば引てけり。猛火は正う押懸たり。喚叫ぶ聲、焦熱、大焦熱、無間阿鼻のほのほの底の罪人も、是には過じとぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: It became night, and it was dark, and the Great General, Prince Taira no Shigehira, stood before the gate of Hōsen-ji, shouting, "Set fire to it!" There was a man in the ranks of the Taira clan, a steward of Fukui Estate in Harima Province, named Jirōtaifu Tomokata, who broke through the shield wall, clung to the pine trees, and set fire to the dwellings. Since it was the night of the 28th of the 12th month, the wind was fierce; though the fire started at one point, the blowing and swirling wind carried it to many temple buildings. Those who cared for their honor and were reluctant to lose their names died in battle at Nara-zaka or were slain at Hōsen-ji. Those who were able to move on foot fled toward Yoshino and the Tenkawa region. Old monks who could no longer walk, ordinary student monks, children, and young nun novices rushed into the Great Buddha Hall and Yamashina-ji, each trying to escape first. On the second floor of the Great Buddha Hall, over a thousand people climbed up, and they pulled up the stairs so that the enemy could not follow. The fierce fire roared fiercely. The cries, the scorching heat, the intense scorching heat—such suffering was not even surpassed by the sinners at the bottom of the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering.

text: 興福寺は淡海公の御願、藤氏累代の寺なり。東金堂に坐ます佛法最初の釋迦の像、西金堂に坐ます自然湧出の觀世音、瑠璃を竝べし四面の廊、朱丹を交へし二階の樓、九輪空に輝きし二基の塔、忽に煙となるこそ悲しけれ。東大寺は常在不滅、實報寂光の生身の御佛と思めし準へて、聖武皇帝、手ら親ら琢き立給ひし金銅十六丈の盧舎那佛、鳥瑟高く顯れて、半天の雲にかくれ、白毫新に拜れ給ひし滿月の尊容も、御頭は燒落て大地に有り、御身は鎔合て山の如し。八萬四千の相好は、秋の月早く五重の雲に掩隱れ、四十一地の瓔珞は、夜の星空く十惡の風に漂ふ。煙は中天に滿々て、炎は虚空に隙もなし。親りに見奉る者、更に眼を當ず、遙に傳聞く人は、肝魂を失へり。法相三論の法門聖教、總て一巻も殘らず。我朝はいふに及ばず、天竺震旦にも、是程の法滅有るべしともおぼえず。優填大王の紫磨金を瑩き、毘首羯摩が赤栴檀を刻じも、纔に等身の御佛なり。況や是は南閻浮提の中には、唯一無雙の御佛、長く朽損の期あるべしとも覺えざりしに、今毒縁の塵に交て、久く悲を殘し給へり。梵釋四王、龍神八部、冥官冥衆も、驚き騒給ふらんとぞ見えし。法相擁護の春日大明神、如何なる事をか覺しけん。されば春日野の露も色變り、三笠山の嵐の音、恨る樣にぞ聞えける。ほのほの中にて燒死ぬる人數をしるいたりければ、大佛殿の二階の上には一千七百餘人、山階寺には八百餘人、或御堂には五百餘人、或御堂には三百餘人、具に記いたりければ、三千五百餘人なり。戰場にして討るゝ大衆千餘人、少々は般若寺の門に切かけ、少々は頸共持せて都へ上り給ふ。

annotation.translation: Kofuku-ji is the temple established by the wish of Prince Tōno-kō, a temple of the Fujiwara clan for generations. In the Eastern Golden Hall sits the first Buddha image of Shakyamuni; in the Western Golden Hall sits the naturally emerging Kannon; the corridors on all four sides are inlaid with lapis lazuli; the two-storied pagoda is decorated with vermilion and cinnabar; the two pagodas with nine rings shine in the sky—oh, how sad that they have suddenly turned to smoke! The Todai-ji Temple, thought to be imperishable and the living Buddha of the Real Land of Quiescence and Light, was sculpted and erected by Emperor Shōmu himself, the great bronze Vairocana Buddha sixteen jō tall, towering majestically, hidden by clouds in the half-sky; the venerable countenance with the new white mark on the forehead, once worshipped as the full moon, now has its head burned off and lies on the earth, and its body is melted like a mountain. The eighty-four thousand marks of perfection are, like the autumn moon, quickly obscured by the five-storied clouds; the forty-one-fold ornaments of the earth are, like the starry night sky, drifting in the wind of the ten evil deeds. The smoke fills the middle sky; the flames leave no gap in the void. Those who have seen it with their own eyes have had their eyes struck; those who have heard of it from afar have lost their souls. The scriptures and teachings of the three doctrines of Dharma Characteristic and Three Treatises have all been destroyed, not even one scroll remaining. Our own nation need not be mentioned; even in India and China, there does not seem to have been such a destruction of the Dharma. The king of Udayana, with his purple molten gold, and Viśvakarma, carving red sandalwood, could only produce a Buddha of life-size. text: 二十九日、頭中將、南都亡して北京へ歸りいらる。入道相國ばかりぞ、憤晴て喜ばれける。中宮一院上皇攝政以下の人々は、「惡僧をこそ滅すとも、伽藍を破滅すべしや。」とぞ御歎有ける。衆徒の頸ども本は大路を渡いて、獄門の木にかけらるべしと、聞えしかども、東大寺興福寺の亡ぬる淺ましさに沙汰にも及ばず。あそここゝの溝や堀やにぞ捨置ける。聖武皇帝の宸筆の御記文には、「我寺興複せば、天下も興複し、我寺衰微せば、天下も衰微すべし。」と遊されたり。されば天下の衰微せん事、疑なしとぞ見えたりける。淺ましかりつる年も暮れ、治承も五年に成にけり。

annotation.translation: On the twenty-ninth day, the Captain General returned to the capital after the Southern Capital had fallen. The Cloistered Retired Emperor and the Great Minister alone felt their anger subside and were pleased. The Empress, the Retired Emperor, the Regent, and all those below them sighed, saying, "Though we should destroy this wicked monk, should we not also destroy the temple?" The heads of the monks were originally to be taken across the main road and hanged on the execution posts, it was heard, but because of the pitiful destruction of the Tōdai-ji and Kōfuku-ji temples, this did not even come to discussion. They were abandoned in the ditches and moats here and there. In the Imperial edict written in the brush of Emperor Shōmu, it was said, "If my temple is revived, the whole world will be revived; if my temple declines, the whole world will decline." Therefore it seemed that there was no doubt that the world would decline. The year, which had been so pitiful, came to an end, and Jishō was also in its fifth year.
